titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Abraham in Egypt, Hagar and Ishmael (ch. 82)
part: ch. 82 — Abraham in Egypt, Hagar and Ishmael
about: In a famine Abraham takes Sarah down to Egypt and has her say she is his sister; Pharaoh takes her, an angel with a sword of fire drives him to restore her, and sends them off with gifts and the maid Hagar. Sarah, still childless, gives Hagar to Abraham and Ishmael is born; after Isaac’s birth she grows jealous, and God tells Abraham to send Hagar and Ishmael away, promising Ishmael a great people and fixing the covenant and the blessing of the nations in Isaac.

sentences.t: ፹፪ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ርደተ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ግብጽ ።
sentences.l: 82. Concerning descent-of Abraham Egypt
sentences.i: Chapter 82: Concerning Abraham’s Descent into Egypt
sentences.n: Chapter heading. በእንተ ‘concerning’ takes the construct state: ርደተ is ርደት ‘descent’ in construct, ‘descent of Abraham’, and ግብጽ ‘Egypt’ follows as the place he goes down to (an accusative of direction, without a preposition). Genesis 12:10–20 is the model for what follows. The number ፹፪ is 82. ግብጽ here is a place name; in unit 15 it is used for the Egyptians as a people.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ናየድዐክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወብዕለ ፡ ኀጥአ ፡ ውሉደ ።
sentences.l: And-again we-shall-inform-you that when gave-him God to-Abraham glory and-wealth, lacked children.
sentences.i: We shall tell you further how, when God had given Abraham glory and wealth, he lacked children.
sentences.n: ወ- ‘and’ begins almost every unit; it is the ordinary narrative joiner, so I note it only where it does more. ወካዕበ ‘and again’; ናየድዐክሙ is a first-person plural imperfect of the causative አየድዐ ‘make known’ with -ክሙ ‘you (pl.)’, ‘we shall make you know’ (?). ወሀቦ ‘he gave him’ is the perfect with the object suffix -ኦ, and the ለ- phrase ለአብርሃም restates the receiver. ክብረ has the -ä ending (construct ‘glory of’ or accusative); nothing follows for it to govern, so it is the plain object ‘glory’, with ወብዕለ ‘and wealth’. ኀጥአ ‘he lacked’ takes ውሉደ ‘children’ as object; the root usually means ‘err, sin’, and ‘lack’ is read from the context (?).

sentences.t: በውስተ ፡ ምስካቢሆሙ ፡ ይትናገሩ ፡ ሳራ ፡ ወአብርሃም ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ ኮንኪ ፡ መካነ ፡ ወይእቲኒ ፡ ትቤሎ ፡ አኮ ፡ አነ ፡ መካን ፡ አላ ፡ አንተ ፤
sentences.l: In-within their-bed speak Sarah and-Abraham, and-he-said-to-her: have-become-you barren; and-she-also said-to-him: not I barren but you;
sentences.i: They were talking together in their bed, Sarah and Abraham, and he said to her, “You have become barren”; and she said to him, “I am not barren, but you are;”
sentences.n: ኮንኪ ‘you (fem.) have become’ (perfect 2fs of ኮነ) with መካነ as the predicate, ‘barren’ (accusative). ‘Barren’ is read from the context (?): መካን usually means ‘place’, and I have not been able to check ‘barren’ in Dillmann. ወይእቲኒ ‘and she also’; አኮ አነ መካን ‘I am not barren’, አላ አንተ ‘but you’. The couple blame each other for childlessness; this exchange is not in Genesis. በውስተ ‘in, within’; ምስካቢሆሙ is ምስካብ ‘bed, lying place’ + -ሆሙ ‘their’ (singular, with the linking vowel before the suffix; ?). ይትናገሩ is the tä-stem imperfect ‘they converse’ (reciprocal). The speech verb recurs: ይቤ ‘he said’ with a suffix, ወይቤላ ‘and he said to her’ (-ላ ‘to her’); ትቤ ‘she said’, ትቤሎ ‘she said to him’ (-ሎ ‘to him’). The ‘said’ verb takes ይ- / ት- prefixes even in the past, so ትቤ has the same shape as ‘you said’ (compare ዘትቤለኒ in unit 13).

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝ ፡ ነበሩ ፡ ይትማከሩ ፡ ይትገአዙ ፡ በበይናቲሆሙ ።
sentences.l: And-on-account-of-this they-were they-take-counsel they-exhort-one-another among-themselves.
sentences.i: On this account they kept taking counsel with one another and urging one another, among themselves.
sentences.n: ወበእንተዝ ‘and on this account’ (በእንተ + the demonstrative ዝ). ነበሩ ‘they were, stayed’ is here an auxiliary: ነበሩ + imperfect gives a continuous sense, ‘they went on taking counsel’. ይትማከሩ ‘they take counsel together’ (tä-stem of መከረ) and ይትገአዙ ‘they urge or constrain one another’ (tä-stem; the root meaning is from context, ?). በበይናቲሆሙ ‘among, between themselves’.

sentences.t: ወቦአ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ከናኦን ፡ ወሰምዐ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ከመ ፡ ቦ ፡ እክል ፡ በብሔረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ፈርዖን ፤
sentences.l: And-entered famine into land-of Canaan, and-heard Abraham that there-is-to-him grain in-land-of Egypt, city-of Pharaoh;
sentences.i: A famine came into the land of Canaan, and Abraham heard that there was grain in the land of Egypt, the city of Pharaoh;
sentences.n: ወቦአ ‘and it entered, came’ (ቦአ, perfect 3ms); ረኃብ ‘famine’ is the subject. ምድረ ‘land of’ is the construct state (ምድር + -ä): a noun followed by another noun gives ‘X of Y’, and the book writes it with ‑ä, so ምድረ ከናኦን ‘land of Canaan’. ከመ ቦ እክል ‘that there is grain’: ቦ is ‘there is to him’, used as ‘there is’; እክል ‘grain’. ሀገረ ‘city of’ is again a construct, in apposition to ብሔረ ግብጽ, ‘land of Egypt, the city of Pharaoh’. Genesis 12:10 has the same famine and the going down to Egypt.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ አኅለቀ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ንዋዮ ፡ በምሒረ ፡ ነዳይ ፡ በመዋዕለ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ኢይናፍቅ ፡ ለጌሠም ፡ ወጸንዐ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ከናኦን ፡ ወኀጥአ ፡ ዘይሴሰይ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ ኣአኵቶ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘወሀበኒ ፡ አኅለቁ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አግብርትየ ፤
sentences.l: And-when finished all his-goods by-mercy-of poor in-days-of famine while not-he-hesitates to-tomorrow, and-grew-strong famine land-of Canaan and-lacked what-one-eats, and-he-said: I-give-thanks to-God who-gave-me; they-finished with my-servants;
sentences.i: When he had spent all his goods in mercy to the poor in the days of famine, not putting it off till the morrow, and the famine grew severe on the land of Canaan and there was nothing to eat, he said, “I thank God who gave to me; they are finished (?), together with my servants;”
sentences.n: A long unit, with three clauses joined by ወ-. ወሶበ ‘and when’ + አኅለቀ ‘he finished, used up’. በምሒረ ነዳይ ‘in mercy to the poor’ takes ምሒረ as a construct of a verbal noun ‘mercy of’ (?), ነዳይ ‘poor man’. እንዘ ኢይናፍቅ ‘while he did not hesitate’ (እንዘ + imperfect gives a circumstantial clause; the verb ናፈቀ is read from context, ?) ለጌሠም ‘till tomorrow’ (ጌሠም ‘morrow’). This is the Kebra Nagast’s own addition (not in Genesis): Abraham gave his wealth to the poor, a pious motive for the descent. ወጸንዐ ‘and it grew strong’; ወኀጥአ ዘይሴሰይ ‘and what one eats failed’ (ዘይሴሰይ ‘that which one eats’, ዘ- relative + imperfect, taken as the subject of ኀጥአ; ‘he lacked food’ is the other possibility, ?). ኣአኵቶ is written with the ኣ and looks like ‘I give thanks to him’ (1cs of አኰተ + -ኦ), taken as ‘I thank (God)’ (?). ዘወሀበኒ ‘who gave me’ (ዘ- + perfect + -ኒ ‘me’). አኅለቁ is a 3mp perfect, ‘they are finished’; its subject is not stated, and I leave it as ‘they’ (?), the phrase ምስለ አግብርትየ ‘together with my servants’ perhaps including the servants in the ruin.

sentences.t: ወባሕቱ ፡ አንቲ ፡ እኅትየ ፡ ሰራ ፡ ኒዒ ፡ ንሖር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ከመ ፡ ናድኅን ፡ ርእስነ ፡ እሞተ ፡ ረኃብ ።
sentences.l: And-but you my-sister Sarah, come, let-us-go to land-of Egypt, that we-save ourselves from-death-of famine.
sentences.i: “But you, my sister Sarah, come, let us go into the land of Egypt, that we may save ourselves from death by famine.”
sentences.n: ወባሕቱ ‘but’; እኅትየ ‘my sister’: Abraham calls his wife ‘sister’ from the start, which quietly prepares the lie of units 9–19 (see Genesis 20:12, where she is also his half-sister). The name is spelled ሰራ here but ሳራ elsewhere; the same woman. ኒዒ is written for ንዒ ‘come!’ (imperative 2fs), ንሖር ‘let us go’ (1cp jussive of ሖረ). ከመ ናድኅን ‘that we may save’: ከመ + a 1cp subjunctive of the causative አድኀነ (‘save’), ርእስነ ‘ourselves’ (lit. ‘our head’). እሞተ ረኃብ ‘from the death of famine’: እም- ‘from’ + construct ሞተ ‘death of’.

sentences.t: ወትቤሎ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ሥምረትከ ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ወእመኒ ፡ ሞትከ ፡ እመውት ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ ወእመኒ ፡ ሐየውከ ፡ አሐዩ ፡ ምስሌከ ፡ ወአልብየ ፡ ዘእትዐደው ፡ እምቃልከ ፡ እስከ ፡ ለዓለም ፨
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-him: let-be your-pleasure, my-lord, and-if you-die I-die with-you, and-if you-live I-live with-you, and-there-is-not-to-me that-I-transgress from-your-word until for-ever.
sentences.i: She said to him, “May it be as you please, my lord. If you die, I will die with you, and if you live, I will live with you, and I will not go beyond your word, for ever.”
sentences.n: ይኩን ‘let it be’ (jussive of ኮነ); ሥምረትከ ‘your pleasure’ (ሥምረት + -ከ ‘your’); እግዚእየ ‘my lord’ (-የ ‘my’), the usual address of a wife to her husband in this chapter. ወእመኒ ‘and if indeed’ (እመ + -ኒ). ሞትከ is the perfect ‘you die’ after ‘if’, and እመውት ‘I die’ the imperfect; so too ሐየውከ ‘you live’ and አሐዩ ‘I live’ (an irregular spelling of the 1cs, ?). ወአልብየ ‘and I have not’ (አልቦ + -የ ‘to me’); ዘእትዐደው ‘that I should go beyond, transgress’ (a relative with the imperfect). እምቃልከ ‘from your word’, እስከ ለዓለም ‘until for ever’. This is Sarah’s vow of obedience, the ground of her later consent; it has no parallel in Genesis 12. The ፨ here, rather than ።, ends a section.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ተንሥኡ ፡ ወአኀዙ ፡ ይሖሩ ፤
sentences.l: And-then they-rose and-began they-go;
sentences.i: Then they rose and began to go;
sentences.n: ወእምዝ ‘and after this, then’. ተንሥኡ ‘they rose’ (tä-stem perfect of ነሥአ, 3mp), ወአኀዙ ‘and they began’ (አኀዘ ‘take hold’, hence ‘begin’ + a following imperfect ይሖሩ ‘they go’): a regular way of saying ‘began to’.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ቀርቡ ፡ ይቤላ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ለሰራ ፡ አሐተ ፡ እሴአለ ፡ ኪ ፡ ወግበሪ ፡ ዘእቤለኪ ፤
sentences.l: And-when they-drew-near he-said-to-her Abraham to-Sarah: one I-ask you and-do what I-say-to-you;
sentences.i: As they drew near, Abraham said to Sarah, “I ask one thing of you, and do what I tell you;”
sentences.n: ወሶበ ‘and when’; ቀርቡ ‘they drew near’ (3mp perfect). ይቤላ ‘he said to her’ and then ለሰራ restates her (the ለ- doubles the suffix, ‘to her, to Sarah’). አሐተ ‘one’ (fem. accusative, ‘one thing’); እሴአለ ኪ is written with a space, for እሴአለኪ ‘I ask you (fem.)’, with -ኪ ‘you’ (2fs); the ending -ለ of እሴአለ is unexplained (?). ግበሪ ‘do!’ (2fs imperative), ዘእቤለኪ ‘what I say to you’. Compare Genesis 12:11–13.

sentences.t: ወትቤ ፡ ሰራ ፡ በል ፡ እግዚእየ ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ አነ ፡ ሰማዕኩ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ሕግ ፡ ንብረቶሙ ፡ በጣዖት ፡ ወበዝሙት ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said Sarah: say, my-lord; and-he-said-to-her: I heard that without law their-way-of-life in-idol and-in-fornication;
sentences.i: Sarah said, “Speak, my lord.” And he said to her, “I have heard that their way of life is without law, in idolatry and fornication;”
sentences.n: በል ‘say!’ (2ms imperative of the irregular ‘say’ verb); ሰማዕኩ ‘I heard’. ዘእንበለ ሕግ ‘without law’ (ዘእንበለ ‘without’); ንብረቶሙ ‘their way of life’ (ንብረት ‘dwelling, manner of living’ + -ሙ ‘their’); በጣዖት ‘in idol-worship’ (ጣዖት is ‘idol’; the worship is implied by the phrase, ?); ወበዝሙት ‘and in fornication’. Genesis 12:12 gives only the fear of being killed for his wife’s beauty; this idolatry and licence is the Kebra Nagast’s own colouring of Egypt.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ርእዩኪ ፡ ላዕሌየ ፡ ይመክሩ ፡ እኩየ ፡ ይቅትሉኒ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ሥነ ፡ ላሕይኪ ፡ እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘይትማሰለኪ ፡ በኀቤሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-when they-see-you upon-me they-plot evil, they-kill-me because-of beauty-of your-face, because there-is-not one-who-resembles-you among-them;
sentences.i: “and when they see you with me, they will plan evil and kill me because of the beauty of your face, for there is none like you among them;”
sentences.n: ላዕሌየ ‘upon me’, which I take here as ‘with me, in my company’ (?). ይመክሩ ‘they plot’ (imperfect); ይቅትሉኒ ‘they will kill me’ (-ኒ ‘me’). ሥነ ላሕይኪ ‘beauty of your face’: ሥነ is construct, ‘beauty of’, and ላሕይኪ ‘your (fem.) face’, ላሕይ ‘appearance, face’ (?). አልቦ ዘይትማሰለኪ ‘there is none who resembles you’ (ዘ- + tä-stem imperfect). በኀቤሆሙ ‘among them’. Genesis 12:11–12 gives the same fear: the Egyptians will see her and kill him.

sentences.t: ወይእዜኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ታሕይዊ ፡ ነፍስየ ፡ በሊ ፡ አንቲ ፡ ለእመ ፡ ተስእሉኪ ፡ በእንቲአየ ፡ በሊ ፡ እኅቱ ፡ አነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ታድኅንያ ፡ ለነፍስየ ፡ እሞት ፡ በእደ ፡ ነኪራን ።
sentences.l: And-now that you-let-live my-soul, say you, if they-ask-you about-me: say: his-sister I, that you-save my-soul, I-die by-hand-of foreigners.
sentences.i: “So now, to keep me alive, if they ask you about me, say, ‘I am his sister,’ so that you save my life; otherwise (?) I shall die at the hands of foreigners.”
sentences.n: ወይእዜኒ ‘and now’. ከመ ታሕይዊ ‘that you (fem.) make live’: ከመ + a 2fs subjunctive of the causative አሕየወ, with ነፍስየ ‘my soul, my life’. በሊ ‘say!’ (2fs imperative); ለእመ ‘if’; ተስእሉኪ ‘they ask you’; በእንቲአየ ‘about me’. ታድኅንያ ‘that you save her’: the -ያ ‘her’ anticipates ለነፍስየ ‘my soul’ (the soul is feminine), the repeated-object pattern with ለ-. እሞት ‘I will die’; በእደ ‘by the hand of’ (construct); ነኪራን ‘foreigners’ (plural of ነኪር). The last clause, እሞት በእደ ነኪራን ‘I die at the hands of foreigners’, has no connective; I read it as the alternative, ‘otherwise I shall die’ (?). This is the request of Genesis 12:13: say she is his sister, that his life may be spared.

sentences.t: ወትቤ ፡ ሳራ ፡ ይኩን ፡ ፈቃድከ ፡ በሊ ፡ ዘትቤለኒ ፡ እብል ፡ ወግበሪ ፡ ዘትቤለኒ ፡ እገብር ።
sentences.l: And-she-said Sarah: let-be your-will; say what you-say-to-me I-say, and-do what you-say-to-me I-do.
sentences.i: Sarah said, “Let it be as you will. I will say whatever you tell me to say, and do whatever you tell me to do.”
sentences.n: ፈቃድከ ‘your will’: ይኩን ፈቃድከ ‘let your will be’, as in unit 7 with ሥምረትከ. ዘትቤለኒ ‘what you say to me’ is ዘ- + the ‘said’ form ትቤ (-ለኒ ‘to me’), here with a present sense, answered by the imperfects እብል ‘I say’ and እገብር ‘I do’. A pointedly obedient Sarah: Genesis 12 gives her no speech at all.

sentences.t: ወበከዩ ፡ ወሰገዲ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወቦኡ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐባይ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ምስር ፤
sentences.l: And-they-wept and-bowed to-God, and-entered into great city-of king-of Egypt;
sentences.i: They wept and bowed down to God, and went into the great city of the king of Egypt;
sentences.n: ወበከዩ ‘and they wept’ is the regular 3mp perfect of በከየ. ወሰገዲ ‘and they bowed’ ends in -ዲ where 3mp ሰገዱ is expected, so I take it as a spelling of ሰገዱ (?). ለእግዚኣብሔር ‘to God’, the object of ‘bowed’ marked by ለ-. ዐባይ I read as ዐቢይ ‘great’ in a variant spelling (?), ‘the great city’; ንጉሠ ምስር ‘king of Egypt’, with ምስር an alternative name for Egypt.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ርእይዎሙ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ወለሳራ ፡ አንከሩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ሥነ ፡ ራእዮሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ ይመስሉ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘተወልዲ ፡ እምአሐቲ ፡ እም ፤
sentences.l: And-when they-saw-them Egypt, Abraham and-Sarah, they-marvelled at-beauty-of their-appearance, because they-resemble as who-were-born from-one mother;
sentences.i: When the Egyptians saw Abraham and Sarah, they marvelled at the beauty of their appearance, for they looked like children born of one mother;
sentences.n: ርእይዎሙ ‘they saw them’ (3mp perfect + -ዎሙ ‘them’); ግብጽ is used here for ‘the Egyptians’ and ለአብርሃም ወለሳራ restates the objects. አንከሩ ‘they marvelled’; ራእዮሙ ‘their appearance’ (ራእይ + -ሙ). ይመስሉ ‘they resemble’ (imperfect pl. of መሰለ); ዘተወልዲ is for ዘተወልዱ ‘who were born’ (tä-stem passive, spelled with -ዲ as ሰገዲ in unit 14, ?), and እምአሐቲ እም ‘of one mother’. So the strong likeness makes the pair seem brother and sister, which the lie turns on. Genesis 12:14–15.

sentences.t: ወይቤልዎ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ምንትከ ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ዛቲ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-said-to-him to-Abraham: what-to-you she this;
sentences.i: They said to Abraham, “What is she to you, this woman?”
sentences.n: ወይቤልዎ ‘and they said to him’ (3mp perfect + -ልዎ ‘to him’), with ለአብርሃም restating. ምንትከ ‘what to you’ (ምንት + -ከ), ይእቲ ዛቲ ‘she, this one’ (fem. pronouns). The questions ask what relation each bears to the other.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎሙ ፡ እኅትየ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-them: my-sister;
sentences.i: He said to them, “My sister.”
sentences.n: The lie, in two words (እኅትየ). Genesis 12:13 and 20:2. The pattern ወይቤሎሙ ‘and he said to them’ (-ሎሙ ‘to them’).

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ተስእልዋ ፡ ለሳራ ፡ ወይቤልዋ ፡ ምንትኪ ፡ ውእቱዝ ፤
sentences.l: And-again they-asked Sarah and-said-to-her: what-to-you this-one;
sentences.i: Again they asked Sarah, and said to her, “What is he to you, this man?”
sentences.n: ወካዕበ ‘and again’; ተስእልዋ ‘they asked her’ (-ዋ ‘her’); ይቤልዋ ‘they said to her’ (-ልዋ ‘to her’). ምንትኪ ‘what to you (fem.)’ and ውእቱዝ ‘he, this one’ (a final -ዝ, perhaps the demonstrative; ?). Separate questioning is the Kebra Nagast’s addition so that the story tallies.

sentences.t: ወትቤሎሙ ፡ እኁየ ፡ ውእቱ ።
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-them: my-brother he.
sentences.i: She said to them, “He is my brother.”
sentences.n: ወትቤሎሙ ‘and she said to them’. እኁየ ‘my brother’ (እኁ ‘brother’ + -የ), with ውእቱ ‘he is’ as copula. The answers agree.

sentences.t: ወበእንተዝ ፡ አርድእዎ ፡ ለፈርዖን ፡ ከመ ፡ መጽኡ ፡ ፪ ፡ አኀው ፡ ሠናያነ ፡ ላሕይ ፡ አሐቲ ፡ ብእሲት ፡ ወ፩ ፡ ወሬዛ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይመስሎሙ ፡ በውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወተፈሥሐ ፡ ፈርዖን ፡ ወለአከ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ሀበኒአ ፡ እኅተከ ፡ ከመ ፡ እሕፅያ ።
sentences.l: And-on-account-of-this they-informed Pharaoh that came 2 brothers good-of face, one woman and-1 lad, and-there-is-not who-resembles-them in-all earth, and-rejoiced Pharaoh and-sent to-him, to-Abraham, saying: give-me your-sister that I-take-in-marriage-her.
sentences.i: Because of this they reported to Pharaoh that two siblings had come, beautiful to look on, one woman and one young man, and that there was none like them in all the earth; and Pharaoh rejoiced and sent to Abraham, saying, “Give me your sister, that I may marry her.”
sentences.n: አርድእዎ ‘they informed him’ (3mp perfect of a causative, + -ኦ), meaning from context (?), with ለፈርዖን restating him. ከመ መጽኡ ‘that they came’. ፪ is the numeral ‘two’ (spoken ክልኤቱ), and ወ፩ ‘and one’. አኀው ‘brothers’ is the plural of አኅ and is used for ‘siblings’; ሠናያነ ላሕይ ‘good ones of face’, a plural accusative adjective with a construct-like noun. ወተፈሥሐ ‘and he rejoiced’ (tä-stem); ወለአከ ሎቱ ለአብርሃም ‘he sent to him, to Abraham’; እንዘ ይብል ‘saying’ (lit. ‘while he says’). ሀበኒአ ‘give me!’ carries a stray final -አ (?): the imperative ሀብ + -ኒ ‘me’, and እኅተከ ‘your sister’. እሕፅያ ‘that I take her’: -ያ ‘her’ on a subjunctive of ሐፀወ ‘take a wife, espouse’ (?). In Genesis 12:15 Pharaoh’s officials praise her and she is taken to his house; here Pharaoh asks Abraham.

sentences.t: ወኀለየ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ለእመ ፡ ከላእኩ ፡ ይቀትለኒ ፡ ወይነሥኣ ፤
sentences.l: And-thought Abraham while he-says: if I-refuse he-kills-me and-takes-her;
sentences.i: Abraham thought, saying, “If I refuse, he will kill me and take her;”
sentences.n: ወኀለየ ‘and he thought’ (ኀለየ ‘think, reckon’); እንዘ ይብል ‘saying’. ለእመ ‘if’ + ከላእኩ ‘I refuse, forbid’ (perfect 1cs, ?); ይቀትለኒ ‘he will kill me’ (-ኒ) and ወይነሥኣ ‘and take her’ (-ኣ). The same fear as unit 11.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ግበርአ ፡ ለእመ ፡ አሥመርከኒ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ጠፋልሐ ፡ ብሩር ፡ ፼ ፡ ወነሥኣ ፡ ለሳራ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይረስያ ፡ ብእሲቶ ፡ ወአእተዋ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ቤቱ ፡ ወአንበራ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ዐራቱ ፡ ወቦአ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ ፈርዖን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ግብጽ ።
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-him: do-it if you-please-me; and-gave-him ጠፋልሐ silver 10,000, and-took Sarah that he-make-her his-wife, and-brought-her-in into his-house and-set-her upon his-bed and-went-in to-her Pharaoh king-of Egypt.
sentences.i: He said to him, “Do it, if you will please me”; and he gave him ጠፋልሐ (?) of silver, ten thousand, and took Sarah to make her his wife, and brought her into his house and laid her on his bed, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, went in to her.
sentences.n: Who speaks in ወይቤሎ ግበርአ is not marked; I read Abraham, who consents on condition of payment, with Pharaoh paying (?). ግበርአ ‘do it!’ (imperative of ገብረ with a stray -አ, ?); ለእመ አሥመርከኒ ‘if you please me’ (causative of ሠመረ ‘be pleased’ + -ኒ ‘me’). ወወሀቦ ‘and he gave him’ (Pharaoh gave). ጠፋልሐ is a word I cannot identify, perhaps a measure or weight of silver (?); ፼ is the Ethiopic sign for 10,000, spoken ዐሠርቱ አእላፍ (?). ወነሥኣ ‘and he took her’; ከመ ይረስያ ብእሲቶ ‘that he make her his wife’: ረሰየ ‘make, appoint’ with -ያ ‘her’ and ብእሲቶ ‘his wife’ in the accusative. ወአእተዋ ‘and he brought her in’ (causative of ወተወ; ?); ዐራቱ ‘his bed’; ወቦአ ኀቤሃ ‘and he went in to her’, a delicate phrase, which the next unit shows did not end in intercourse. Compare Genesis 12:16 (gifts to Abram) and 12:15.

sentences.t: ወአስተርአዮ ፡ መልአከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ በሌሊት ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይጸውር ፡ ሰይፈ ፡ እሳት ፡ ወቀርበ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ ወአብርሀ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እምነበልባሉ ፡ ወፈቀደ ፡ ይቅትሎ ፤
sentences.l: And-appeared-to-him angel-of God by-night while he-carries sword-of fire, and-drew-near to-him and-lit house from-his-flame and-wished he-kill-him;
sentences.i: An angel of God appeared to him in the night, carrying a sword of fire, and came close to him and lit the house with its flame, and wished to kill him;
sentences.n: አስተርአዮ ‘he appeared to him’ (the causative-reflexive አስተርአየ ‘be seen’ + -ኦ ‘to him’); መልአከ እግዚኣብሔር ‘angel of God’, a construct chain; ሰይፈ እሳት ‘sword of fire’, another. The image of a flaming sword recalls the cherubim’s sword at the gate of Eden (Genesis 3:24). ወአብርሀ ‘he lit up’ (causative of በርሀ); እምነበልባሉ ‘from his flame’ (እም- ‘from’, here the source of the light; ነበልባሉ ‘his flame’); ወፈቀደ ይቅትሎ ‘and he wished to kill him’. In Genesis 12:17 the LORD afflicts Pharaoh with plagues; here it is an angel.

sentences.t: ወጐየ ፡ ፈርዖን ፡ እምአረፍተ ፡ ቤት ፡ እስከ ፡ አረፍተ ፡ ቤት ፡ ወእማእዝንተ ፡ ቤት ፡ እስከ ፡ ማእዝንተ ፡ ቤት ፡ ወኀበ ፡ ሖረ ፡ ይተልዎ ፡ ወኀጥአ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ይትገመር ፡ ወኀበ ፡ ይትኀባእ ።
sentences.l: And-fled Pharaoh from-wall-of house to wall-of house, and-from-corner-of house to corner-of house, and-where he-went it-followed-him, and-lacked where he-be-covered and-where he-hide.
sentences.i: Pharaoh fled from one wall of the house to another, and from one corner of the house to another, and wherever he went the angel pursued him, and he had nowhere to take cover or hide.
sentences.n: ወጐየ ‘and he fled’; እምአረፍተ ቤት እስከ አረፍተ ቤት ‘from the side/wall of the house to the side of the house’ (አረፍተ construct, the meaning ‘wall, side’ taken from context, ?); ማእዝንተ ‘corner of’ (construct). ወኀበ ሖረ ይተልዎ ‘and where he went it followed him’ (ኀበ ‘where’; ይተልዎ, imperfect of ተለወ ‘follow’ + -ኦ ‘him’). ወኀጥአ ኀበ ይትገመር ‘he lacked a place where he might be covered’ (ይትገመር, tä-stem, ?) ወኀበ ይትኀባእ ‘and where he might hide’. The repetition (‘from X to X’) conveys the endless chase.

sentences.t: ወእምዝ ፡ ሰፍሐ ፡ እደዊሁ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ለመልአክ ፡ ኅድግ ፡ ሊተ ፡ ዛተ ፡ አበሳየ ፡ እግዚኦ ።
sentences.l: And-then stretched-out his-hands and-said-to-him to-angel: forgive me this my-sin, O-lord.
sentences.i: Then he stretched out his hands and said to the angel, “Forgive me this sin of mine, Lord.”
sentences.n: ሰፍሐ እደዊሁ ‘he stretched out his hands’ (እደው ‘hands’, plural of እድ, + -ሁ ‘his’). ኅድግ ሊተ ‘leave to me, forgive me’ (imperative 2ms of ኀደገ + ሊተ ‘to me’); ዛተ አበሳየ ‘this my sin’ (-የ ‘my’); እግዚኦ ‘O lord’ (vocative, here to the angel).

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ ለምንት ፡ ትገፍዕ ፡ ብእሲቶ ፡ ለብእሲ ።
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-him: why do-you-wrong his-wife to-man.
sentences.i: The angel said to him, “Why do you wrong a man’s wife?”
sentences.n: ለምንት ‘why’ (ለ- + ምንት ‘what’). ትገፍዕ ‘you wrong, oppress’ (2ms imperfect); ብእሲቶ ለብእሲ ‘the wife of a man’, a doubled possessive: the suffix -ሁ on the noun is answered by the ለ- phrase, literally ‘his wife, to a man’. Compare Genesis 12:18, where Pharaoh reproaches Abram for what he has done.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ኢትቅትል ፡ ደመ ፡ ንጹሐ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-him: O-lord, do-not-kill blood innocent;
sentences.i: He answered, “Lord, do not kill innocent blood;”
sentences.n: ወይቤሎ here is Pharaoh speaking. ኢትቅትል ‘do not kill’ (ኢ- + 2ms jussive); ደመ ንጹሐ ‘innocent blood’, ንጹሐ the accusative adjective. The idiom ‘innocent blood’ is biblical (Deuteronomy 19:10).

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ይቤለኒ ፡ እኅትየ ፡ ወበእንተዝ ፡ አነ ፡ ሐፀይክዋ ፡ በንጹሕ ፤
sentences.l: because he-said-to-me my-sister, and-on-account-of-this I took-her-in-marriage in-innocence;
sentences.i: for he told me she was his sister, and so I married her in innocence;
sentences.n: እስመ ‘because’; ይቤለኒ ‘he said to me’, with እኅትየ ‘my sister’ as the quotation. ሐፀይክዋ ‘I took her to wife’ (perfect 1cs of ሐፀወ + -ዋ ‘her’; ?) በንጹሕ ‘in innocence’. This is Pharaoh’s defence, as in Genesis 12:19, where he asks Abram why he said she was his sister, so that he took her to wife.

sentences.t: ወምንተ ፡ እግበር ፡ ከመ ፡ እድኀን ፡ እምእዴከ ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ አግብእ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ለአብርሃ ፡ ም ፡ ብእሲቶ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ ዐስበ ፡ ወፈንዎ ፡ በሰላም ፡ ይእቱ ፡ ብሔሮ ።
sentences.l: And-what shall-I-do that I-be-saved from-your-hand; and-he-said-to-him: return to-him, to-Abraham, his-wife, and-give-him wages and-send-him in-peace he his-country.
sentences.i: “And what am I to do to be saved from your hand?” And the angel said to him, “Give Abraham back his wife, and give him a reward, and send him away in peace to his own country (?).”
sentences.n: ወምንተ እግበር ‘and what shall I do’; ከመ እድኀን ‘that I be saved’; እምእዴከ ‘from your hand’ (እም- + እድ + -ከ). አግብእ ‘return, give back’ (imperative of the causative አግብአ) with ሎቱ ለአብርሃ ም ‘to him, to Abraham’: the name is split by a space (አብርሃ ፡ ም) and is one word, Abraham. ወሀቦ ‘give him’ (imperative ሀብ + -ኦ) and ዐስበ ‘a reward, wages’; ፈንዎ ‘send him’ (imperative + -ኦ). በሰላም ‘in peace’. ይእቱ ብሔሮ I read as ‘to his own country’ (?): ብሔሮ ‘his country’ with a pronoun-like ይእቱ before it that I cannot explain. Genesis 12:19–20 has Pharaoh summon Abram and send him away himself.

sentences.t: ወሶቤሃ ፡ ጸውዖ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ሳራ ፡ ብእሲቶ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አመት ፡ እንተ ፡ ስማ ፡ አጋር ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ወብሩረ ፡ ወአልባሰ ፡ ክቡረ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ ወፈነዎ ፡ በሰላም ፨
sentences.l: And-then he-summoned Abraham and-gave-him Sarah his-wife with maidservant who her-name Hagar, and-gave-him gold and-silver and-garments precious to-Abraham, and-sent-him in-peace;
sentences.i: Then he summoned Abraham and gave him Sarah his wife, with a maidservant named Hagar, and gave Abraham gold and silver and costly garments, and sent him away in peace;
sentences.n: ወሶቤሃ ‘and then, at that time’; ጸውዖ ‘he called him’. ወወሀቦ ሳራ ብእሲቶ ‘and he gave him Sarah his wife’ (two objects). ምስለ አመት እንተ ስማ አጋር ‘with a maidservant whose name is Hagar’: እንተ is the feminine relative, ስማ ‘her name’, አጋር is Hagar. In Genesis 16:1 Hagar is Sarai’s Egyptian slave-girl; this makes her Pharaoh’s gift at the Egyptian court. አልባሰ ክቡረ ‘costly garments’ (plural of ልብስ, and the accusative adjective). Compare Genesis 12:16, where the gifts are sheep, oxen, asses, servants, camels. The ፨ ends a section.

sentences.t: ወገብኡ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሀገሮሙ ።
sentences.l: And-they-returned into their-country.
sentences.i: And they returned to their own country.
sentences.n: ወገብኡ ‘and they returned’ (perfect 3mp of ገብአ); ሀገሮሙ ‘their country’. Genesis 13:1 has Abram go up to the Negeb.

sentences.t: ወትቤሎ ፡ ሳራ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ አእመርኩ ፡ አነ ፡ ከመ ፡ መካን ፡ አነ ፡ ወባሕቱ ፡ ባእ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ አመትየ ፡ እንተ ፡ ወሀበኒ ፡ ፈርዖን ፡ እመ ፡ ይሁበከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘርአ ፡ በውስቴታ ፤
sentences.l: And-she-said-to-him Sarah to-Abraham: I-knew I that barren I; and-but enter to this my-maidservant whom gave-me Pharaoh, perhaps may-give-you God seed in-her;
sentences.i: Sarah said to Abraham, “I know that I am barren; but go in to this maidservant of mine, whom Pharaoh gave me, in case God may give you offspring through her;”
sentences.n: አእመርኩ ‘I have known’ (perfect 1cs of አእመረ); ከመ መካን አነ ‘that barren am I’. ባእ ኀበ ‘enter to’ (ባእ imperative of ቦአ), a euphemism for lying with her; ዛቲ አመትየ ‘this my maidservant’, እንተ ወሀበኒ ፈርዖን ‘whom Pharaoh gave me’. እመ ይሁበከ ‘perhaps he will give you’ (እመ ‘if, whether’ + subjunctive, ?); ዘርአ ‘seed’ (offspring), በውስቴታ ‘in her’. Genesis 16:2 has the same proposal. In Genesis Sarai’s proposal comes after ten years in Canaan; here it comes at once, with Hagar as Pharaoh’s gift.

sentences.t: ወአንሰ ፡ ቀበጽኩ ፡ ርእስየ ፡ ወተነግፈ ፡ ወየብሰ ፡ ጽጌ ፡ ከርሥየ ።
sentences.l: And-as-for-me I-despaired myself, and-was-cut-off and-dried flower-of my-belly.
sentences.i: As for me, I have lost hope, and the flower of my womb has been cut off (?) and has dried up.
sentences.n: ወአንሰ ‘and as for me’ (አነ + emphatic -ሰ). ቀበጽኩ ርእስየ ‘I (have) despaired, myself’ (the verb ቀበጸ ‘be lost, lose hope’, ?; ርእስየ ‘my head, myself’). ወተነግፈ is a tä-stem perfect ‘was cut off, withdrawn’ (?); it seems to share ጽጌ ከርሥየ as its subject with የብሰ (?). ወየብሰ ጽጌ ከርሥየ ‘and the flower of my womb dried’: የብሰ ‘was dry’; ጽጌ ‘flower’ in construct before ከርሥየ ‘my womb’ (ከርሥ ‘belly’, here ‘womb’).

sentences.t: ወወሀበቶ ፡ አጋር ፡ ወቦአ ፡ ኀቤሃ ፡ ወፀንሰት ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ወወለደት ፡ ወሰመየቶ ፡ ስሞ ፡ እስማዔል ፤
sentences.l: And-she-gave-him Hagar, and-he-went-in to-her, and-she-conceived to-him and-bore, and-she-named-him his-name Ishmael;
sentences.i: So she gave Hagar to him, and he went in to her, and she conceived by him and bore a son, and she named him Ishmael;
sentences.n: ወወሀበቶ አጋር ‘and she gave him Hagar’: ወሀበቶ is the 3fs perfect + -ቶ ‘him’ (the book’s spelling of -ኦ after a fem. verb), with አጋር the object. ወቦአ ኀቤሃ ‘and he went in to her’. ወፀንሰት ሎቱ ‘and she conceived for him’; ወወለደት ‘and she bore’; ወሰመየቶ ስሞ እስማዔል ‘and she named him his name Ishmael’ (ሰመየ ‘name’; ስሞ ‘his name’ doubles the object). This chapter spells the name እስማዔል here and ይስማዔል later (unit 36, etc.); one name. In Genesis 16:11 the angel tells Hagar to name the child Ishmael, and 16:15 has Abram name him; here Sarah names him.

sentences.t: ሰምዐኒ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ብሂል ፨
sentences.l: He-heard-me God, saying.
sentences.i: That is, “God has heard me.”
sentences.n: ሰምዐኒ እግዚኣብሔር ‘God heard me’ (perfect + -ኒ ‘me’); ብሂል ‘saying, that is’ (verbal noun of ብህለ), the usual gloss-marker after a name. It explains the name Ishmael (Hebrew yišmāʿēl, ‘God hears’), as in Genesis 16:11, where the angel gives the name together with its reason.

sentences.t: ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እምነ ፡ ሳራ ፡ ብእሲቱ ፡ ወወለደ ፡ ይስሐቅ ፡ ወእምድኅሬሁ ፡ ቀንአት ፡ ሳራ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ይስማዔል ፡ ወልደ ፡ አመታ ፡ እስመ ፡ ልህቀ ፡ እምቅድመ ፡ ወልዳ ፤
sentences.l: And-after-him gave-him seed God from Sarah his-wife and-begot Isaac, and-after-him was-jealous Sarah on-account-of Ishmael son-of her-maidservant because he-grew from-before her-son;
sentences.i: After this God gave him offspring by Sarah his wife, and he begot Isaac; and afterwards Sarah grew jealous of Ishmael, her maidservant’s son, because he had grown up before her own son;
sentences.n: ወእምድኅሬሁ ‘and after him, afterwards’ (ድኅሬ + -ሁ), twice; ወሀቦ ዘርአ እግዚኣብሔር ‘God gave him seed’; እምነ ሳራ ‘from Sarah’. ወወለደ ይስሐቅ ‘and he begot Isaac’ (the spelling ይስሐቅ here, ይስሓቅ later). ቀንአት ‘she was jealous’ (3fs perfect); ወልደ አመታ ‘son of her maidservant’ (ወልደ construct, አመታ ‘her maidservant’). ልህቀ ‘he grew, grew great’; እምቅድመ ወልዳ ‘before her son’, lit. ‘from before’. Genesis 21:2–3, 9. The elder son’s precedence in age makes the quarrel.

sentences.t: ትቤ ፡ ዮጊ ፡ ይቀትሎ ፡ ለወልድየ ፡ ወይወርስ ፡ ቤተ ፡ አቡሁ ።
sentences.l: She-said: ዮጊ (perhaps?) he-kills my-son and-inherits the-house-of his-father.
sentences.i: She said, “Perhaps (?) he will kill my son and inherit his father’s house.”
sentences.n: ዮጊ is a word I cannot identify; I take it as an adverb of possibility, ‘perhaps, indeed’ (?), as it stands before a subjunctive; the glossary entry for the form reads ‘then (?)’, so both readings are guesses. ይቀትሎ ለወልድየ ‘he kills him, my son’ (the suffix -ኦ answered by ለወልድየ). ወይወርስ ቤተ አቡሁ ‘and inherits the house of his father’: ቤተ is the construct. Genesis 21:10 has Sarah object that the slave woman’s son shall not share the inheritance with Isaac; here the fear is murder.

sentences.t: ወሦዐ ፡ መሥዋዕተ ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይቤ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ምንተ ፡ እግበር ፡ በእንተ ፡ ይስማዔል ፡ ወልድየ ፡ ቀዳሜ ፡ በኵርየ ፤
sentences.l: And-offered sacrifice-of Abraham to-God, and-he-said: O-lord, what shall-I-do about Ishmael my-son first-of my-firstborn;
sentences.i: Abraham offered a sacrifice to God and said, “Lord, what shall I do about Ishmael my son, first of my firstborn?”
sentences.n: ወሦዐ is a contracted spelling for ወሠውዐ ‘and he sacrificed’ with መሥዋዕተ ‘sacrifice’ (the -ä form, accusative or construct ‘sacrifice of’; it stands before አብርሃም, so I read ‘Abraham offered a sacrifice’, with ‘Abraham’s sacrifice’ as the other possibility, ?). ምንተ እግበር ‘what shall I do’, በእንተ ‘about’. ቀዳሜ በኵርየ ‘first, my firstborn’, ቀዳሜ construct ‘first of’, so literally ‘first of my firstborn’; ‘my first, my firstborn’ is the looser sense. Genesis 21:11 says the matter greatly displeased Abraham on account of his son.

sentences.t: አነ ፡ እፈቅድ ፡ ይሕየወኒ ፡ ቅድ ፡ ሜከ ፡ ወሳራ ፡ እኅትየ ፡ ትቀንእ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘወሀብከኒ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ በርሥኣኒ ፡ እስመ ፡ ኮኖ ፡ ለይስማዔል ፡ ፲ወ፬ ፡ ዓመት ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ይትወለድ ፡ ይስሓቅ ።
sentences.l: I I-want he-live-for-me before-you, and-Sarah my-sister is-jealous on-account-of the-seed you-gave-me in-my-old-age, because it-was-to Ishmael 14 years before was-born Isaac.
sentences.i: “I want him to live for me before you, while Sarah my sister is jealous because of the offspring you gave me in my old age (?), for Ishmael was fourteen years old before Isaac was born.”
sentences.n: እፈቅድ ‘I wish’ (imperfect) + a following subjunctive ይሕየወኒ ‘that he live for me’ (-ኒ as a dative ‘for me’); ቅድ ሜከ is for ቅድሜከ ‘before you’, split by a space (?). ወሳራ እኅትየ ‘and Sarah my sister’: Abraham calls his wife ‘sister’ also here (see unit 6). ትቀንእ ‘she is jealous’; ዘወሀብከኒ ዘርአ ‘the seed which you gave me’; በርሥኣኒ I take as ‘in my old age’ (?), a noun (the word is uncertain, and -ኒ is ‘me’ on a verb, not a usual ‘my’ on a noun, so the parse is doubtful, ?). እስመ ኮኖ ለይስማዔል ፲ወ፬ ዓመት ‘for it was to Ishmael fourteen years’: ኮኖ is ኮነ ‘it was’ with -ኦ ‘to him’; ፲ወ፬ is 14, spoken ዐሠርቱ ወአርባዕቱ. ዘእንበለ ይትወለድ ይስሓቅ ‘before Isaac was born’ (ዘእንበለ + a tä-stem subjunctive). Abraham was 86 at Ishmael’s birth (Genesis 16:16) and 100 at Isaac’s (21:5), so the figure fourteen is right.

sentences.t: ወይቤሎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ አማን ፡ ዘትቤ ፡ ሳራ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-said-to-him God to-Abraham: truth what she-said, Sarah;
sentences.i: God said to Abraham, “What Sarah said is true;”
sentences.n: አማን ‘truth, truly’; ዘትቤ ሳራ ‘what Sarah said’ (the prefix form serves as the perfect, as in unit 2) (ዘ- + the 3fs ትቤ). Genesis 21:12 has God tell Abraham to listen to Sarah.

sentences.t: ስድዳ ፡ ለአመት ፡ ምስለ ፡ ወልዳ ፡ ይስማዔል ፤
sentences.l: Send-away the-maidservant with her-son Ishmael;
sentences.i: “send away the maidservant with her son Ishmael;”
sentences.n: ስድዳ ‘drive her out, send her away’ (imperative 2ms of ሰደደ + -ኣ ‘her’), ለአመት ‘the maidservant’ restated with ለ-. ወልዳ ‘her son’. Genesis 21:10, 12–14.

sentences.t: ወለይስማዔልሰ ፡ ኅድጎ ፡ ይሕየው ፡ ቅድሜየ ፡ ወአነ ፡ እሬስዮ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ ዐቢየ ፡ ወይወልድ ፡ ፲ወ፪ ፡ ሕዝበ ፡ ወይነግሥ ፡ ላዕሌሆሙ ፤
sentences.l: and-as-for-Ishmael, leave-him he-live before-me, and-I I-make-him people great, and-he-begets 12 peoples and-reigns over-them;
sentences.i: but as for Ishmael, leave him to live before me, and I will make of him a great people; he will beget twelve peoples and reign over them;
sentences.n: ወለይስማዔልሰ ‘and as for Ishmael’ (ለ- fronting the topic, + emphatic -ሰ). ኅድጎ ‘leave him!’ (imperative + -ኦ); ይሕየው ቅድሜየ ‘let him live before me’ (ቅድሜየ ‘before me’). እሬስዮ ‘I will make him’ (1cs of ረሰየ + -ኦ) ሕዝበ ዐቢየ ‘a great people’. ፲ወ፪ is 12, spoken ዐሠርቱ ወክልኤቱ. Genesis 17:20 promises Ishmael twelve princes and a great nation; 21:13, 18 repeat the great nation. Here they become twelve peoples who live under his rule.

sentences.t: ወኪዳንየሰ ፡ ኣቀውም ፡ ምስለ ፡ ይስሓቅ ፡ ገብርየ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ሳራ ፡ ወእባርክ ፡ በዘርኡ ፡ ኵሎሙ ፡ አሕዛበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወእገብሮ ፡ ዐበይተ ፡ ነገሥተ ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ አሕዛበ ፡ ምድር ፡ ወበሰማያትኒ ፡ እሬስዮ ፡ ንጉሠ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-my-covenant I-establish with Isaac my-servant son-of Sarah, and-I-bless in-his-seed all peoples-of earth, and-I-make-him great kings over all peoples-of earth, and-in-heavens-also I-make-him king.
sentences.i: “But my covenant I will establish with Isaac my servant, the son of Sarah, and in his seed I will bless all the peoples of the earth; and I will make him great kings over all the peoples of the earth, and in the heavens too I will make him king.”
sentences.n: ወኪዳንየሰ ‘and as for my covenant’ (ኪዳን + -የ ‘my’ + -ሰ); ኣቀውም ‘I will establish’ is written with ኣ, a 1cs form of አቀመ (?). Genesis 17:21 has God establish the covenant with Isaac. ወእባርክ በዘርኡ ኵሎሙ አሕዛበ ምድር ‘I will bless in his seed all the peoples of the earth’, the promise of Genesis 22:18 (and 12:3), with አሕዛበ the construct ‘peoples of’. ወእገብሮ ዐበይተ ነገሥተ ‘I will make him great kings’ (?): the object is Isaac, and ‘great kings’ I read as his line of kings (?). በሰማያትኒ ‘in the heavens also’ (plural ሰማያት + -ኒ), where I read Christ’s heavenly kingship, the point towards which the Kebra Nagast’s genealogies run (?). The ፨ ፨ ፨ … row at the end closes the chapter and stays with this unit.
